 Order No. 04 Dated 08th May, 2025  I.A. No. 5436 of 2025 Heard the learned counsel for the respective parties.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable u/s 363, 366 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of the I.P.C. and Sections 4/6 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced for R.I. for 20 years along with a fine of Rs. 10,000/- for the offence u/s 6 of the POCSO Act r/w 5(1) of the POCSO Act.
It has been alleged that the appellant had enticed away the daughter of the informant and had taken her to a deserted place and had established physical relationship with her.
It has been submitted by Mr. Singh, learned counsel appearing for the appellant that the evidence of the victim who has been examined as PW-2 clearly reveals that there was a love affair between the victim and the appellant which resulted in her leaving her home willingly and allowing the appellant to establish physical relationship with her.
It has further been submitted that the medical report does not support the factum of rape as no external or internal injuries were found on the person of the victim.
Learned APP has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
On consideration of the evidence of PW-2 it clearly transpires that the appellant had committed rape upon the victim.
In view of the above, therefore, we are not inclined to consider the prayer for bail of the appellant which stands rejected.
